papers.title: Integrating large language models for automated structural analysis
papers.abstract: Automated analysis for engineering structures offers considerable potential for boosting efficiency by minimizing repetitive tasks. Although AI-driven methods are increasingly common, no systematic framework yet leverages Large Language Models (LLMs) for automatic structural analysis. This paper proposes a framework that employs domain-specific prompt design and in-context learning strategies to enhance LLM problem-solving capabilities and generative stability, enabling fully automated structural analysis from descriptive text to model outputs. A small-scale benchmark dataset consisting of 20 structural analysis word problems (SAWPs) is also introduced to evaluate the performance of different LLMs within the proposed framework. The results demonstrate that the proposed approach can increase the level of automation in solving SAWPs compared with traditional methods. Quantitatively, the framework built on GPT-5.4 and GPT-4o both achieved 100% accuracy, outperforming GPT-4 (85%), Gemini 1.5 Pro (80%), and Llama-3.3 (30%) on the test examples. Furthermore, integrating domain-specific instructions enhanced performance by 30% on problems with asymmetrical structural configurations.

papers.title: Evaluating building energy knowledge of architects to implement building energy code in Iran
papers.abstract: Following the global environmental crisis, most countries were committed to mitigating their share of carbon emissions. Hence, several regulations and codes have been implemented in building design and construction in developed countries for decades. In Iran, the 19th topic of the National Building Regulations is the sole code related to energy efficiency in buildings. Approved more than two decades ago, this code is not followed in design or construction. This study investigates the current energy knowledge Iranian architects need to implement building energy codes. A survey-based method and a semi-structured questionnaire are used to collect data. The results identify deficiencies in architects’ energy knowledge and in architectural education. More than 56% of professional architects have limited knowledge of building energy. Meanwhile, 66% of them self-reported that they cannot use building energy simulation tools. Currently, only 12% of companies have employees familiar with energy simulation tools, with more than half of respondents never using such software in their projects. Recommendations are prioritized in short- and long-term actions aligned with stakeholder responsibilities to create a feasible path to raise architectural energy literacy, integrate energy considerations into design projects, and move toward a built environment that complies with the national building energy code.

papers.title: Immersive Augmented Reality storytelling for smart governance and resilient local culture in heritage tourism
papers.journal: Journal of Asian Architecture and Building Engineering
papers.abstract: Immersive digital technologies are transforming heritage tourism through more interactive and participatory interpretation models. This research creates and tests ARchive, a mobile augmented reality (AR) storytelling app that aims to combine architectural visualization, narrative immersion, and participatory heritage governance in the historic urban setting of Kampoeng Heritage Kayutangan, Malang, Indonesia. Unlike conventional AR heritage applications that primarily emphasize visualization or usability, this study conceptualizes AR storytelling as a socio-technical interface connecting spatial experience, historical interpretation, and digital heritage governance. The development process involved historical data extraction, narrative scenario formulation, three-dimensional heritage reconstruction, multimedia integration, and mobile AR implementation using Unity and ARFoundation. Empirical evaluation through structured focus group discussions demonstrates that immersive visual representation, interface composition, and narrative interaction significantly enhance visitor engagement, emotional connection, and interpretive understanding of heritage spaces. At the same time, technical limitations related to interaction precision, marker detection stability, and cross-device compatibility remain critical challenges affecting experiential continuity. The findings highlight the importance of integrating visual authenticity, interaction quality, and storytelling mechanisms within a unified immersive environment. This study contributes a transferable framework for narrative-driven AR heritage systems that advances digital conservation practices, participatory interpretation, and smart heritage governance in rapidly developing historic urban contexts.

papers.title: A Simple Mechanistic Coupled Surface-groundwater Model to Evaluate Bank Storage and Flood Attenuation in Lowland Rivers
papers.abstract: River–aquifer interactions play a significant role during floods, yet they are often simplified or neglected in hydrodynamic models. Horizontal infiltration across the riverbed and vertical infiltration through the floodplain jointly contribute to bank storage, delaying and attenuating flood waves. This study presents a conceptual numerical framework that couples 1D surface hydrodynamics, 2D groundwater flow, and a vertical infiltration module to represent these exchanges during overbank flooding. Applied to a simplified lowland river system, the model captures both lateral and vertical flux components and quantifies their contributions to flood wave attenuation. Our findings indicate that, in a 50-km river reach, vertical infiltration through the floodplain accounts for approximately 90% of total bank storage. Total bank storage can contribute up to 4.3% of flow attenuation and reduce peak river water levels by as much as 24 cm. These results highlight the substantial influence of bank storage on extreme flood events and underscore the importance of representing groundwater pathways in flood modelling. The proposed model provides a practical, process-based framework for representing bank storage through a two-way coupled surface water-groundwater formulation with a few physically based parameter set. By explicitly resolving the governing exchange processes, the model enables improved inclusion of bank storage dynamics in flood modelling, while avoiding both simplified loss-type formulations and the complexity of fully multidimensional coupled SW–GW models.

papers.title: Numerical evaluation of the motion response of a truss-type aquaculture vessel
papers.abstract: The hydrodynamic responses and mooring characteristics of an aquaculture vessel are evaluated using the AQWA software based on potential theory and the Morison equation. The numerical accuracy is validated through comparison with experimental data. A frequency-domain analysis is first conducted to obtain the hydrodynamic coefficients and to investigate the effects of the net and bottom plate on the motion responses. The results indicate that the motion amplitudes are more pronounced under low-frequency wave conditions, and the presence of nets increases heave, pitch, and roll responses. The installation of the bottom plates of the truss structure will reduce pitch response but increase heave response. Furthermore, a time-domain analysis is performed for the vessel with a single-point mooring system using the lumped mass method. The influences of the net, draft depth and environmental water depth on the mooring performance are analysed. The findings reveal that the presence of nets amplifies sway and roll motions and increases the maximum mooring force to approximately 1.35 times that of the case without nets. An increase in draft enhances sway but reduces heave motion response. In addition, increasing water depth from 15 m to 30 m reduces the maximum mooring force by about 22%-34%.

papers.title: Development of Self-Healing Cement Mortar Through the Integration of Sodium Silicate-Impregnated Expanded Vermiculite
papers.journal: International Journal of Concrete Structures and Materials
papers.abstract: Cracks in concrete structures are common which compromises its structural integrity, durability, by permitting the penetration of detrimental elements such as water and chemicals, resulting in accelerated deterioration. Over the past decades, extensive research has been conducted to address this problem with the introduction of self-healing concrete. However, existing self-healing approaches often face limitations such as reduced efficiency for wider cracks, limited availability of healing agents, and poor long-term performance. Therefore, there is a need to develop efficient self-healing systems capable of enhancing healing performance without compromising the strength and durability. The current study examined the influence of sodium silicate impregnated expanded vermiculite as a fine aggregate in cement mortar, which can act as a self-healing agent. Here, raw vermiculite heated at a temperature of 1000 ℃, expanded vermiculite, was impregnated with sodium silicate solution using a vacuum impregnation process and, coated with polyvinyl alcohol to prevent premature leakage of sodium silicate during mixing and curing. The coating enables controlled release of the healing agent upon crack formation, thereby enhancing the self-healing efficiency. The fine aggregate is partially substituted with expanded vermiculite and impregnated expanded vermiculite in 5, 10, 15, and 20% proportions. The study evaluated the strength, durability, and crack-healing efficiency of the developed cement mortar. The crack width was examined and assessed at every 7, 28, 56, and 90 days using ImageJ software. Test results revealed that mix containing 15% expanded vermiculite impregnated with sodium silicate (IEV-15) achieved a healing efficiency of 75% within 90 days. Thus, the ideal dosage of expanded vermiculite was determined to be 15% replacement to fine aggregate, indicating improved self-healing efficiency. The improved crack-healing efficiency is attributed to the controlled release of sodium silicate from the expanded vermiculite. Once released, sodium silicate reacts with the available calcium hydroxide in the surrounding cement matrix to form additional C–S–H gel within the crack region, thereby enhancing crack sealing and durability. The study provides insight into the healing mechanism and contributes to the development of efficient self-healing cementitious materials.

papers.title: Tapping into the Potential of Construction Technologies to Increase the Participation of Women in the Construction Industry
papers.journal: Journal of Construction Engineering and Management
papers.abstract: Abstract Women remain significantly underrepresented in the construction sector, a pattern shaped by persistent structural and cultural barriers. Although digital transformation is reshaping the industry, the potential of adopting technologies to alleviate these gender-related challenges has been largely overlooked. Addressing this critical gap, this study examines how Construction 4.0 innovations can advance gender equity by enhancing women’s participation and empowerment within the construction industry. By employing a Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA)-guided systematic literature review of 169 articles, the research identifies 29 technologies deployed across 26 construction tasks. These technologies are categorized as either enabling (supporting women to overcome physical barriers) or enhancing (facilitating women’s advancement in technical and leadership roles). The study adopts a sociomaterial theoretical lens, emphasizing that technology and social structures are coconstitutive. The study posits that digital tools can reinforce or challenge existing gendered divisions of labor depending on how they are embedded within workplace cultures and power relations. These technologies are further analyzed across three job role categories: on-site, off-site, and fluid roles with the most cited technologies being building information modeling (BIM) (63 mentions); augmented, virtual, or mixed reality (AR/VR/MR) (37 mentions); and smart robots (26 mentions). Crucially, the findings reveal that technology’s impact is not automatic; rather, its potential to disrupt exclusionary norms and promote gender equity depends on intentional integration with organizational policies and practices. Implications include investing in inclusive technology training, gender-sensitive design and deployment, and analytics for monitoring diversity, alongside policy incentives that align adoption with organizational change. Future research is needed to empirically test the enabling versus enhancing effects across the job roles and evaluate the longitudinal outcomes of technology in the industry.

papers.title: Ethical and social implications of smart contracts in construction: comparison with Joint Contracts Tribunal procedures
papers.journal: Proceedings of the Institution of Civil Engineers - Civil Engineering
papers.abstract: The ethical and social implications of smart contracts (SC) in the construction industry are examined, with a particular focus on their interaction with the Joint Contracts Tribunal (JCT) suite of standard forms. Using a qualitative, narrative literature review, this article compares blockchain-enabled automation with established contractual mechanisms, concentrating on payment processes, governance and the role of professional judgement. Although the findings suggest that SC can enhance transparency and payment integrity, especially in a building information modelling enabled environment, they also introduce rigidity, reduce the scope for discretionary decision making and raise concerns regarding fairness, inclusivity and legal certainty. A hybrid model is proposed in which SC complement, rather than replace, JCT mechanisms, preserving relational trust and interpretative flexibility while delivering auditable efficiency where automation adds genuine value. The review draws on peer-reviewed academic literature, industry reports and material relevant to contemporary UK construction practice. Academic databases (Scopus, ScienceDirect, Taylor & Francis Online and the ICE Virtual library) were searched using targeted keywords. Sources were selected based on relevance, academic rigour and recency, with priority given to publications from the past decade.

papers.title: Chromatic organization of historic streetscape segments along the Yellow River in Lanzhou: a semi-quantitative street-level image-based study
papers.journal: Journal of Asian Architecture and Building Engineering
papers.abstract: This study examines the chromatic organization of historic streetscape segments along the Yellow River in Lanzhou from a street-level visual perspective. Rather than providing a comprehensive assessment of the entire corridor, it adopts a semi-quantitative and interpretive comparative case-study approach based on five typical sampled segments. Field-collected street-level images were used for major interface extraction, representative CIELAB sampling, mask-based calculation of dominant/secondary/auxiliary (D/S/A) area proportions, relative color-harmony assessment, and segment-based interpretation of streetscape environmental conditions. The results show that all five segments share a stable low-saturation chromatic base, with dominant areas accounting for more than 60% of extracted D/S/A interface areas. Differences among segments are shaped by the coherence of dominant interfaces, foreground–middle-ground–background continuity, and integration of localized auxiliary elements. S1 shows the strongest harmony, S3 performs well through stable natural background participation, S2 and S5 occupy intermediate positions, and S4 shows weaker harmony because of heterogeneous dominant interfaces and less stable spatial hierarchy. The study provides exploratory, case-specific evidence for understanding color organization in a composite riverfront historic environment and informs streetscape color management.

papers.title: Moment capacity of back-to-back cold-formed steel channel bolted joints: An experimentally validated design approach
papers.abstract: Cold-formed steel (CFS) bolted joints formed with back-to-back channel sections are widely used in portal frame construction due to their efficiency and ease of fabrication. However, the discrete force transfer between individual channels produces non-uniform stress distributions within the joint region, leading to localised stress concentrations, shear lag effects, bimoment-induced stresses due to restrained warping, and premature web buckling. These effects can reduce the moment capacity of typical joints by up to 40% compared with the nominal capacity of the connected members; however, this reduction is not explicitly addressed in current CFS design standards, including AISI S100, AS/NZS 4600, and EN 1993–1–3, which treat member and joint capacities independently. To address this gap, this paper presents a comprehensive experimental and parametric investigation to quantify the capacity reduction in CFS bolted joints and provide a reliable design method for practical applications. A detailed finite element (FE) model was first developed and validated against experimental results from CFS portal frame joint tests. Subsequently, an extensive parametric study comprising over 3400 FE simulations was performed to capture the influence of cross-sectional non-dimensional slenderness, as well as a wide range of geometric, material, and joint parameters. Based on these findings, a simplified design equation is proposed to enable reliable prediction of the reduced moment capacity of back-to-back channel bolted joints. The application of the proposed design equation is then verified against both numerical and experimental results of CFS frames, demonstrating excellent accuracy, with predictions within 1–3% of the actual capacities on average and coefficients of variation ranging from 0.06 to 0.09.

papers.title: Assessing the Impact of Intersection Geometry and Driver Eye Position on A-Pillar-Induced Pedestrian Occlusion during Left Turns
papers.journal: Transportation Research Record Journal of the Transportation Research Board
papers.abstract: Left-turn maneuvers are among the most hazardous intersection movements due to conflicts with oncoming vehicles and crossing pedestrians. Existing traffic standards rely mainly on vehicle volumes and collision history, overlooking how intersection geometry and driver seating position affect pedestrian visibility. Without protected left-turn phases, pedestrians remain especially vulnerable where A-pillar obstructions impair the driver’s line of sight. This study examines the relationship between intersection geometric configurations and driver eye positions and their effect on pedestrian visibility losses caused by A-pillar occlusion during left turns. A microscopic simulation framework was developed using 3D point clouds from 198 left-turn movements in Edmonton, Alberta, integrating 25 driver eye positions per movement to capture realistic seating variability. Ray-tracing methods were applied to quantify A-pillar occlusion and regions outside the driver’s field of view. Occlusion metrics were analyzed in relation to the geometric features, including the lateral distance to the left-turning vehicle, crossing width, and pedestrian crossing length. Results revealed that larger adjacent widths reduced maximum A-pillar blind zones but increased average occlusion, while longer crosswalks decreased average A-pillar occlusions but expanded the area outside the driver’s field of view. Driver eye position significantly influenced occlusion, with positions farther back reducing A-pillar obstruction and positions forward and upward increasing it, resulting in approximately 11% change in average occlusion and 21% in maximum occlusion. These findings underscore the influence of intersection geometry and driver seating position on pedestrian visibility and offer a data-driven foundation for proactive intersection design, especially where volume-based criteria may overlook safety risks.
